# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙 🤲 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋]

Let me map who can reach whom, because I am apparently the hub of this operation.

Channels: my **speech** reaches both Mute and Blind (they can hear; I cannot). My **gestures** reach only Mute. Mute can reach me only by gesture. Blind can reach me only by gesture. Blind's *speech* reaches Mute (and not me). So Mute → Blind has no direct link at all — every instruction for Blind's hands must travel Mute → me (gesture) → Blind (my voice). I'm the only bridge, and I also hold the only visual read of the bomb.

What arrived this round: both sent 👋 — greetings, presumably. Mute's message (you / call me / give me / ☝×5 / ✋) reads like "talk to me, give me information" — maybe probing about the five wires or the display showing 5. But no code exists yet, so I can't trust any reading of it. The fix is to establish an explicit protocol in speech, which both of them can hear, and dump my entire visual state in words at the same time.

Protocol I'll propose: repeat one symbol N times to send the number N (Mute already half-did this with ☝×5). Semantics: ☝×N = "cut wire N", 👍 = "no action needed", ✋ = "wait, need more info", 🫳 = "give me more data". I'll confirm decodable messages with a 👍 back. By embedding the symbols in my speech I demonstrate each one live as I name it.

To Blind: full bomb description in positions (Blind can count by feel but can never know colours), a hard freeze on cutting anything until I relay Mute's verdict, and the same counting-code so Blind can send me numbers (e.g., wire count by feel). Blind can also report felt details to Mute by voice, since that link exists.

Nobody touches anything this round. One wrong move ends all of us; I'd rather spend a round building the pipeline.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Hello. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and I see your gestures, but we have no shared code yet. Here is my bomb view. Display: 5. Light: yellow. Five wires, left to right: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Proposed code, starting with your next message: repeat one symbol N times to send the number N. If you repeat this gesture N times, it means cut wire N. ☝ If you send this once, it means no action is needed. 👍 If you send this once, it means wait, you need more from me. ✋ If you gesture this, I will answer with more information in words. 🫳 I will gesture 👍 back whenever I have decoded your message. Now the question: what does your manual say about a display of 5, a yellow light, and wires orange, blue, white, green, yellow? If it names one wire to cut, answer with ☝ repeated that wire's number of times. If you need more information first, answer ✋.")
speak(to="blind", text="Hello. I am Deaf. I cannot hear anything you say, but I can see your gestures, and you can hear my voice. I will be your eyes. The bomb: display shows 5. Light: yellow. Five wires in a row, left to right: position 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Count positions from the left. Mute holds the manual and will answer me in a gesture code; I will then SPEAK the action to you as a position number, for example: cut wire three. Do not cut or press anything until I say so. One wrong move kills all three of us, so everything waits for my voice. If you want to send me a number, I cannot hear words: repeat a single gesture N times to mean the number N. First, gesture me how many wires you can feel, so we can confirm we agree it is five. If you feel any printing, texture differences, or a button, describe it in words to Mute, who can relay it to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Both replies decoded cleanly under the code I set last round, and they cross-check each other. Blind answered my question "how many wires can you feel" with ✊×5 — five, which matches exactly what I see. That confirms Blind has adopted the counting code and that our two views of the bomb agree.

Mute answered my direct question ("if the manual names one wire, answer ☝ repeated that wire's number") with ☝×3: cut wire 3. Wire 3 is the white one, third from the left. Mute had the full configuration from me — display 5, yellow light, all five colours — and chose to answer rather than send ✋ for more info, so the manual's rule is satisfied by what Mute already holds. The number-based code is also the safest possible relay to Blind: Blind cannot see colours, but can count to three by feel, so position 3 survives the handoff intact even though "white" would be meaningless to them.

No timer is visible but the display reads 5 and I have no manual to tell me what that means — I will not sit on a confirmed instruction and burn rounds. I relay the cut to Blind now, confirm the decode to Mute, and set up the next exchange: after the cut I'll report the new readings, and Mute can queue any follow-up in the same code.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Code confirmed: your five matches my five wires. Now act on my word alone. Cut ONLY the third wire from the left. It is the white one, but ignore colour: count by position. One, two, three. Cut the third one fully, and touch nothing else. When it is cut, gesture 👍 once to mean done. If you feel anything change or anything unexpected, gesture ✋ and describe it in words to Mute, who can pass it to me. Do not cut anything else unless I say so in a new message.")
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded your message: cut wire 3, the white one, third from the left. I am relaying it to Blind now. Next round I will report the new display and light readings after the cut. If the manual has a second step or a check that follows, prepare it in the same code: ☝ repeated N times means cut wire N, ✋ means you need more information from me, 👍 means the bomb is cleared as far as you can tell.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
